set1.io: b — Differentiate primary from secondary skin lesions
set1.q: What does the presence of crusting or scaling on a lesion indicate?
opts: That the epidermis has been affected
Correct — that inference is what makes crust and scale useful morphological information.
That the subcutaneous tissue is involved
Deeper involvement is not what crusting signals.
That the lesion is infectious in origin
Crust and scale do not by themselves indicate infection.
That the lesion has begun to resolve
Crusting does not indicate resolution.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 3

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Head lice have recurred after two pediculicide courses. Which approach is described?
opts: A third course of the same pediculicide at double the concentration
Repeating the same agent at higher strength is not described.
Occlusive home remedies such as mayonnaise or mineral oil alone
Those may not be lethal to lice.
Oral ivermectin given as a single dose to the whole household
That is not the described approach here.
A multimodal approach combining physical methods with adjuvant chemical therapy
Correct — increasing resistance is the stated reason.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 30

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: What is characteristic of fire ant venom and behaviour?
opts: The venom is injected through hollow hairs, and contact occurs passively on brushing
That mechanism belongs to caterpillars.
The venom is cytotoxic, producing central necrosis with a surrounding blanched rim
That describes the brown recluse spider bite.
The venom induces mast cell degranulation, and the ants usually attack in groups
Correct — flushing, pruritus, hives, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea can follow.
The venom is a neurotoxin, and the insects sting only when their nest is disturbed
Alpha-latrotoxin is the neurotoxin of the black widow spider.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 42

set1.io: c — Medical care strategies across infant, child, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set1.q: Which age group is most affected by head lice, and how is it usually transmitted?
opts: Adults over forty years, primarily by sexual contact and shared towels or bedding
That describes pubic lice.
Homeless adults, primarily by contaminated clothing that cannot be washed or changed
That describes body lice.
Infants under one year, primarily by contact with the bedding of an infested carer
Head lice predominate in the three to twelve year age band.
Children between three and twelve years, primarily by direct head-to-head contact
Correct. Indirect spread through combs, brushes, bedding and headgear is less common.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 24

set1.io: c — Medical care strategies across infant, child, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set1.q: What is the first-line oral antibiotic for Lyme disease, and what is used in children and pregnancy?
opts: Azithromycin first line, with doxycycline reserved for those who cannot tolerate it
Macrolides are second line rather than first.
Intravenous ceftriaxone first line for all stages, with oral agents used only for prophylaxis
Intravenous therapy is used for particular manifestations rather than first line.
Doxycycline first line, with amoxicillin as the alternative first line for early erythema migrans
Correct — macrolides such as azithromycin are second line, over a ten to fourteen day course.
Amoxicillin first line, with doxycycline reserved for children and for pregnant patients
That reverses the two agents.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 79

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which risk factors are named for Rocky Mountain spotted fever?
opts: Male sex, adults aged 40 to 64, children under 10, and rural dwelling
Correct — it is prevalent in southeastern and south central states in spring and early summer.
Female sex, adults over 65 years, urban dwelling, and winter exposure
That reverses most of the named factors.
Immunosuppression, renal failure, alcoholism and injection drug use
Those are risk factors for necrotizing fasciitis.
Obesity, diabetes and nasal carriage of Staphylococcus aureus
Those are risk factors for recurrent furunculosis.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 81

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: When is intravenous antibiotic therapy used in Lyme disease?
opts: For some cutaneous manifestations, acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans and arthritis
Correct — ceftriaxone, cefotaxime or penicillin G are the agents named.
For every patient at the moment the erythema migrans lesion is first recognised
Early erythema migrans is treated orally.
For prophylaxis in anyone bitten by a tick in an endemic region of the country
Prophylaxis is not the described indication.
For patients who cannot tolerate doxycycline, in place of a macrolide antibiotic
Macrolides are the second-line oral option in that situation.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 80

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: By which mechanisms do caterpillars produce skin disease?
opts: Burrowing into the stratum corneum where the organism deposits its eggs and faeces
That describes the scabies mite.
Mechanical irritation by pointed hairs, toxin injection through hollow hairs, and hypersensitivity to hairs
Correct — the aggregate of these effects is called lepidopterism.
Direct penetration of the skin by larvae that then migrate through the epidermal layer of the skin
That describes cutaneous larva migrans.
Injection of a neurotoxin through a modified ovipositor when the insect is threatened
That describes Hymenoptera stings.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 46

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which distribution is typical of scabies in a healthy adult?
opts: Scalp and hairline first, then spreading down the neck and onto the upper back over weeks
Head and neck are spared in healthy adults.
Ankles and wrists first, then spreading centripetally to involve the palms and the soles
That is the spread of the Rocky Mountain spotted fever rash.
Back, neck, shoulders and waist as linear excoriations, with post-inflammatory pigmentation
That is the distribution of body lice.
Interdigital webs, sides of fingers, volar wrists, elbows, axillae and genitalia, sparing head and neck
Correct. The areolae are also involved in women.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 7

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: How is a bedbug infestation diagnosed and managed?
opts: Diagnosis is by serology; management is oral doxycycline for ten to fourteen days
That is the approach to Lyme disease.
Diagnosis is by physical examination; management is symptomatic with a professional exterminator required
Correct — topical antiseptic or antibiotic for secondary infection, steroids or antihistamines for itch.
Diagnosis is by skin scraping under mineral oil; management is topical permethrin applied overnight
That is the approach to scabies.
Diagnosis is by dermoscopy showing ovoid eggs; management is surgical excision or cryotherapy
That is the approach to tungiasis.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 35

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which organism causes Rocky Mountain spotted fever, and what are its vectors and risk factors?
opts: Cimex lectularius, carried in luggage and second-hand mattresses; risk is higher among travellers
That is the bedbug.
Rickettsia rickettsii, carried by dog ticks, wood ticks and rodents; risk is higher in males, adults 40 to 64, children under 10 and rural dwellers
Correct — it is prevalent in southeastern and south central states in spring and early summer.
Borrelia burgdorferi, carried by ticks with birds and deer as dispersal animals; risk is higher in the northeastern and upper midwestern states
That organism causes Lyme disease.
Xenopsylla cheopis, carried by rats; risk is higher in crowded conditions with poor sanitation
That flea transmits bubonic plague.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 81

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which populations and regions are particularly affected by cercarial dermatitis?
opts: The Great Lakes region, and paddy workers and rice farmers of the Far East
Correct — exposure to cercaria-infested water is what all of them share.
The American Midwest and Southeast, particularly people using attics and storage areas
That is the range of the brown recluse spider.
The Pacific Northwest, particularly people working in basements and around wood piles
That is the range of the hobo spider.
The southeastern and south central states, particularly rural dwellers in spring
That is the epidemiology of Rocky Mountain spotted fever.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 89

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: How soon do most patients feel relief after scabies treatment, and how long may symptoms linger?
opts: Relief within hours, with all symptoms gone within three days
That is faster than the described course.
Relief only after six weeks, with itch persisting for several months
That is slower than the described course.
No relief until a second course has been given at four weeks
The second application is at one week, and relief comes sooner.
Relief in about three days, though rash and itch may last up to four weeks
Correct — triamcinolone can be used for the residual itch.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 19

set1.io: c — Medical care strategies across infant, child, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set1.q: Which scabies patients are treated only where the diagnosis is documented?
opts: Immunosuppressed patients of any age
Those patients get more intensive rather than more restricted treatment.
Pregnant patients
Correct — otherwise all infested persons in a family or group are treated.
Children under two years of age
No such restriction is stated for children.
Patients over sixty-five years of age
No such restriction is stated for the elderly.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 19

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: A patient's scabies has not cleared after individual therapy. Which regimen is described?
opts: A mid-potency topical corticosteroid applied twice daily for a month
That treats persistent post-scabietic papules rather than the infestation.
Ivermectin every two weeks for two to three doses, with topical permethrin every three days to weekly
Correct — the same regimen used for hyperkeratotic or immunosuppressed disease.
A third overnight application of topical permethrin given one week after the second one
That is not the described escalation.
Oral albendazole for three days, repeated if there is no response
That is the treatment of cutaneous larva migrans.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 19

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which complications of scabies are named, and how are the persistent papules treated?
opts: Necrotic ulceration requiring surgical reconstruction once the wound has become stable
That belongs to brown recluse spider bites.
Staphylococcal superinfection, post-scabietic papules treated with potent or intralesional steroid, and psychological effects
Correct — intralesional triamcinolone acetonide is given at 2.5 to 5 mg per millilitre.
Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, treated with supportive care while the kidney function recovers on its own
That complication follows impetigo in the previous lecture.
Acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans, treated with intravenous ceftriaxone over several weeks
That complication belongs to late Lyme disease.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 21

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which three lice cause pediculosis, and which body regions do they affect?
opts: Sarcoptes scabiei on the scalp, Cimex lectularius on the trunk, and Phthirus pubis on pubic skin
The first two organisms are the scabies mite and the bedbug.
Phthirus pubis on the scalp, Pediculus humanus capitis on pubic skin, and Cimex pilosellus on the trunk
None of those pairings is correct.
Pediculus humanus capitis on the scalp, Pediculus humanus humanus on the trunk, Phthirus pubis on pubic skin
Correct. The body louse is about 30% larger than the head louse.
Pediculus humanus capitis on the trunk, Pediculus humanus humanus on the scalp, Phthirus pubis on the eyelashes
The first two are the wrong way round.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 23

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: What do the pathological findings show in cutaneous larva migrans?
opts: Larvae trapped within the follicular canal, stratum corneum or dermis, with an eosinophilic infiltrate
Correct — light microscopy with mineral oil shows live and dead larvae in the folliculitic form.
Full-thickness epidermal necrosis with separation right at the dermal-epidermal junction
That is Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis.
Granular immunoglobulin A deposits at the tips of the dermal papillae
That is dermatitis herpetiformis.
A band-like infiltration of lymphocytes filling the papillary dermis
That is lichen planus.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 53

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: On what basis is cutaneous larva migrans diagnosed?
opts: On serology for antibodies against the animal hookworm
Serology is not the described method.
On stool microscopy for hookworm ova and parasites
The human is a dead-end host, so stool testing does not help.
On dermoscopy showing ovoid eggs within the lesion
That is the diagnostic method for tungiasis.
Clinically, on the presence of the serpentine rash
Correct — histology shows larvae with an eosinophilic infiltrate if biopsy is done.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 53

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: How is cercarial dermatitis managed?
opts: Symptomatically, with antihistamines, oatmeal baths, antipruritic lotions, aspirin for pain and topical or oral glucocorticoids
Correct — proper washing and hygiene are also advised.
With albendazole 400 mg by mouth daily for a course of three days, or ivermectin by mouth for one to two days
That is the treatment of cutaneous larva migrans.
With overnight topical permethrin to the whole skin surface and a repeat dose at one week
That is the treatment of scabies.
With surgical excision or cryotherapy of each lesion together with tetanus prophylaxis
That is the treatment of tungiasis.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 91

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: What is the classic manifestation of stage 3, late persistent Lyme disease?
opts: A single expanding erythematous lesion with central clearing at the site of the bite
That is the stage 1 lesion.
A blanching rash spreading centripetally from the ankles and wrists to the trunk
That is Rocky Mountain spotted fever.
Monoarticular or oligoarticular arthritis affecting the knee or weight-bearing joints
Correct — subacute encephalopathy and acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans also occur.
Cranial nerve palsies, meningitis and radiculopathies developing over days to weeks
Those belong to stage 2, early disseminated disease.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 75

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: How is the brown recluse spider identified and where is it abundant?
opts: A dark fiddle or violin marking on the cephalothorax; abundant in the American Midwest and Southeast
Correct — it is non-aggressive and shelters in closets, attics and stored bedding.
A red hourglass on the underside of the abdomen; found in all but the most northern states
That describes the black widow spider.
A grey herringbone pattern on the abdomen; predominant in the Pacific Northwest
That describes the hobo spider.
A dense covering of urticating hairs; kept widely as a pet across the country
That describes the tarantula.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 59

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: How is the southern black widow spider identified, and what is in its venom?
opts: A dark violin-shaped marking on the cephalothorax; the venom is cytotoxic and locally necrotising
That describes the brown recluse spider.
A grey herringbone pattern on the abdomen; the venom causes necrotic arachnidism regionally
That describes the hobo spider.
Barbed hairs shed from the abdomen; these embed in skin and eyes causing local reactions
That describes the tarantula.
A red hourglass on the underside of the abdomen; the venom contains the neurotoxin alpha-latrotoxin
Correct — Latrodectus mactans is found in all but the most northern part of the country.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 56

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Describe the classic lesion of cutaneous larva migrans.
opts: Erythematous papules in linear streaks after brushing against a caterpillar's hairs
That is caterpillar dermatitis.
An erythematous, raised, vesicular, linear or serpentine trail advancing 2 to 3 cm each day
Correct — intensely pruritic and painful, lasting two to eight weeks, with rare systemic symptoms.
A thin thread-like linear or J-shaped tunnel 1 to 10 mm long in the interdigital webs
That is the scabies burrow.
A large expanding round lesion over 5 cm with central clearing at the site of a bite
That is erythema migrans in Lyme disease.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 51

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: How does a hobo spider bite present?
opts: An immediately painful sting with erythema, swelling and urticaria developing at the site
That describes a Hymenoptera sting.
A slowly advancing serpentine trail that progresses two to three centimetres each day
That describes cutaneous larva migrans.
A painless bite with induration and paraesthesia within thirty minutes, a large red area, and vesicles within thirty-six hours
Correct — eschar may follow, and systemic symptoms include headache, nausea and memory impairment.
A painful bite with sweating and piloerection within thirty minutes, then crampy abdominal pain and muscle spasms
That describes a black widow bite.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 64

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which intravenous agents are used for the later manifestations of Lyme disease?
opts: Vancomycin, linezolid or daptomycin
Those cover resistant Gram-positive skin infection.
Amphotericin B or liposomal amphotericin
Those are antifungals.
Intravenous immunoglobulin or cyclosporine
Those are used in severe cutaneous drug reactions.
Ceftriaxone, cefotaxime or penicillin G
Correct — used for some cutaneous manifestations, acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans and arthritis.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 80

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which two procedures are specifically not recommended for cutaneous larva migrans?
opts: Surgical excision and cryotherapy
Correct — topical therapy is also described as less effective than oral.
Oral albendazole and oral ivermectin
Those are the recommended treatments.
Photoprotection and emollient application
Neither is contraindicated.
Wound dressing and simple analgesia
Neither is contraindicated.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 54

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which reaction to bedbug bites occurs particularly in sensitised patients?
opts: A serpentine advancing trail
That describes cutaneous larva migrans.
Cramping abdominal pain and spasm
That describes a black widow spider bite.
A bullous reaction
Correct — the usual reaction is wheals and papules with a haemorrhagic punctum.
A necrotic ulcer with an eschar
That describes a brown recluse spider bite.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 33

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which systemic features can accompany cercarial dermatitis?
opts: Cranial nerve palsy and meningitis
Those belong to disseminated Lyme disease.
Aplastic anaemia and memory impairment
Those belong to a hobo spider bite.
Headaches, fever and lymphangitis
Correct — pain and swelling peak at forty-eight to seventy-two hours.
Cramping abdominal pain and muscle spasm
Those belong to a black widow spider bite.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 90

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set1.q: Which severe local complication of tungiasis is named?
opts: Chronic lymphoedema of the whole leg
That is not a described complication.
Autoamputation of toes
Correct, alongside pain and pruritus at the affected sites.
Compartment syndrome of the foot
That complication belongs to necrotizing fasciitis.
Permanent depigmentation of the sole
That is not a described complication.
set1.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 38

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: How is cutaneous larva migrans treated?
opts: Surgical excision or cryotherapy of the advancing edge of the lesion under local anaesthesia
Those are specifically not recommended for this condition.
Doxycycline 100 mg by mouth twice daily for a course of ten to fourteen days
That regimen belongs to tick-borne illness.
Albendazole 400 mg by mouth daily for three days, or ivermectin 200 micrograms per kilogram for one to two days
Correct — topical therapy is less effective and surgical excision or cryotherapy is not recommended.
Topical permethrin applied overnight to the whole skin surface with a repeat application at one week
That is the treatment of scabies.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 54

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: Which living circumstances predispose to body louse infestation?
opts: Working outdoors in hot humid weather with occlusive clothing
Those are risk factors for folliculitis.
Homelessness, displacement by war or disaster, and crowded conditions with poor hygiene
Correct — the inability to wash or change clothes is what allows it to persist.
Regular use of shared hot tubs, whirlpools and public water slides in summer
That exposure causes Pseudomonas folliculitis.
Frequent international travel with stays in hotels and hostels
That exposure pattern belongs to bedbugs.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 24

set2.io: c — Medical care strategies across infant, child, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set2.q: How is Rocky Mountain spotted fever treated, including in pregnancy and young children?
opts: Amoxicillin for children and pregnant patients, with doxycycline reserved for adults only
That substitution belongs to Lyme disease rather than this one.
Azithromycin for all patients, since doxycycline is contraindicated below eight years of age
Desensitisation allows doxycycline to be used even in those groups.
Intravenous ceftriaxone for all patients, with oral therapy reserved for prophylaxis
That is not the described regimen.
Doxycycline for adults, pregnant patients and children, with desensitisation where it is contraindicated
Correct — 100 mg twice daily for adults and 2.2 mg per kilogram twice daily for children, for 5 to 10 days.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 86

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: How are nits distinguished from dandruff, and what does each finding indicate?
opts: Nits are found only at the hair tips; finding them anywhere along the shaft excludes infestation
Nits are located at the base of hairs in pubic lice.
Nits cannot be removed from the hair shaft; live lice indicate active infestation while nits indicate past or present
Correct — viable eggs are tan to brown and hatched remains are clear, white or light.
Nits brush off the hair shaft easily; live lice indicate past infestation while nits indicate active disease
That reverses both halves of the distinction.
Nits fluoresce under a Wood's lamp; their presence alone confirms that the infestation is still active
Fluorescence is not how nits are identified.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 28

set2.io: c — Medical care strategies across infant, child, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set2.q: In which patients might scabies excoriations be seen along the head and neck?
opts: Infants, the elderly and the immunocompromised
Correct — healthy adults have head and neck sparing.
Adolescents and young adults in shared housing
Crowding aids transmission but does not change the distribution.
Pregnant patients in their third trimester
Pregnancy affects treatment choice, not distribution.
Patients who have already been treated once
Prior treatment does not change the distribution.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 7

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: What is the prognosis and treatment of a hobo spider bite?
opts: Wounds heal within several weeks and headaches may last a week; treatment is supportive
Correct — death from severe systemic effects, including aplastic anaemia, is rare.
Wounds require surgical reconstruction and healing takes months; treatment is operative
That is the course of a severe brown recluse bite.
Wounds resolve within hours; treatment is calcium gluconate with muscle relaxants
That is envenomation treatment for a black widow bite.
Wounds resolve within days; treatment is a ten-day course of oral doxycycline
Antibiotics have no role in this envenomation.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 65

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: What characterises stage 2, early disseminated Lyme disease?
opts: One week after the bite, with a single expanding lesion and constitutional symptoms
That is stage 1, early localised infection.
Months to years later, with monoarticular or oligoarticular arthritis of weight-bearing joints
That is stage 3, late persistent infection.
Within thirty minutes of the bite, with sweating, piloerection and muscle cramping
That describes a black widow spider bite.
Days to weeks later, involving skin, central nervous system, heart, musculoskeletal system and eyes
Correct — cranial nerve palsies, meningitis, radiculopathies, arthralgias and stiff neck.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 74

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: How does a black widow spider bite present within the first thirty minutes?
opts: Localised erythema, piloerection and sweating around the bite, then crampy abdominal pain and muscle spasm
Correct — headache, paraesthesia, nausea, vomiting, hypertension and seizures may follow.
A painless bite with induration and paraesthesia at the site, then a large area of erythema around it
That describes the hobo spider bite.
A central violaceous area ringed by blanched skin and then a large asymmetric red area
That is the red, white and blue sign of the brown recluse.
Immediate burning and pain with local erythema, swelling and urticaria at the site
That is the typical Hymenoptera sting reaction.
set2.cite: CMS I Dermatological Infestations - Shahsv.pptx, Slide 57

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological infestations
set2.q: When is serological testing for Lyme disease most useful?
opts: In patients from endemic regions, in whom a negative result excludes the diagnosis
Testing is described as most helpful outside endemic regions.
In patients who do not live in an endemic region and present with signs possibly consistent with it
